name: AD 1052 Candidate Event

phenomena.details: A smaller, weaker 14C production peak flagged by Brehm et al. (2021) as a candidate solar particle event, awaiting multi-archive confirmation.

impacts.description: If solar in origin, a modest enhancement of atmospheric radiocarbon production; substantially weaker than the confirmed AD 774 and AD 993 events.

papers.title: Eleven-year solar cycles over the last millennium revealed by radiocarbon in tree rings
papers.authors: Brehm, N., Bayliss, A., Christl, M., et al.
papers.keyFinding: Flagged AD 1052 and AD 1279 as two new, smaller candidate production events in an annually resolved AD 969-1933 radiocarbon record, distinct from the confirmed AD 993 event.

summary: A candidate, unconfirmed solar particle event near AD 1052, seen as a small radiocarbon production peak in a single tree-ring record and awaiting independent corroboration.
description: Brehm et al. (2021) identified AD 1052 as one of two smaller candidate production peaks (with AD 1279) in their annually resolved AD 969-1933 atmospheric radiocarbon record, alongside the confirmed AD 993 event. The signal is markedly weaker than the firmly established events and currently rests largely on a single 14C record without the multi-archive, multi-continent corroboration (independent tree-ring chronologies plus 10Be and 36Cl in ice cores) that confirmed AD 774 and AD 993. Alternative explanations, including astrophysical sources or broader solar-modulation structure, have been discussed. It is included here as a candidate pending confirmation.
